_about: Pollster register for the Times poll tracker. One entry per firm. Wording fields are verbatim from the firm's own data tables unless the *_source field says otherwise. Audited 13 Nov 2026 from the files archived in data/poll-tracker/raw/ (SHA256SUMS there). Edit this file by hand; scripts/build_register.py writes the flat CSV summary.
_inclusion_rules: R1 Full tables published within a few days (the BPC disclosure standard, applied as a test whether or not the firm is a member)
R2 Standard GB Westminster voting intention question (no MRP, constituency, regional or propensity-scale polls)
R3 Not commissioned by a party or campaign group
R4 Active: at least 3 standard VI polls in the last 90 days

pollsters.name: More in Common
pollsters.bpc_evidence: Tables cover page: "More in Common is a member of the British Polling Council and abides by its rules"
pollsters.weighting_text: Respondents have been weighted according to age/sex interlocked, region, 2024 General Election vote, ethnicity, and education level.
pollsters.turnout_question: If a general election was called tomorrow, how likely would you be to vote? Please rate from 0 to 10, where 0 means certain not to vote, and 10 means certain to vote.
pollsters.turnout_threshold: 8/10 or above; 9/10 or above if did not vote at the last general election
pollsters.vi_question: And, if a general election was called tomorrow, which party would you vote for?
pollsters.squeeze_question: If you were forced to choose, which party would you vote for?
pollsters.dk_text: Undecided voters are asked a follow-up question of how they would vote if forced to choose, and those who are still undecided in this question are assigned to a party using a statistical model based on how they compare to similar voters.

pollsters.tables_format: xlsx (one sheet per question: likelihoodtovote, votingintention, votingforced, votingintention (headline))
pollsters.reuse_terms: Not checked (site terms page not read)
pollsters.scrape_notes: Single archive page lists every xlsx with fieldwork dates. Sheet names are stable and named after the question variable. Shares stored as unrounded proportions. Implemented via the WordPress media API; many old polls were re-uploaded in Apr-May 2026 and special-topic VI files (hypothetical, regional, 'pop music' etc.) share the naming, so the scraper filters by name and requires a headline sheet.

Option order shown to respondents (Restore Britain sits last in tables, which may mean it was added later rather than shown last)

pollsters.name: Deltapoll
pollsters.method_note_summary: Relaunched VI in May 2026 after a post-2024 pause. Combines several survey waves with exponentially declining weights on older waves, so each poll partly reuses earlier respondents. Also uses a new turnout model adjusting for how reliably different groups report their likelihood to vote.
pollsters.scrape_notes: Polls library (/polls-library, paginated, not in date order). VI polls are /polls/voteint-YYMMDD but some appear under other slugs (burnham-260521, burnham-260616, burnham-260721, voter-concerns-260506 for the Mirror), so pages tagged voting intention/politics/Labour are opened too and the PDF decides. Layouts vary poll to poll; crossbreak columns read from each page's header against a vocabulary, Total only when they don't fit. Hypothetical 'with Andy Burnham as Labour leader' tables stored as separate questions (stage vi_hypothetical). The page's 'Date Published' can precede fieldwork, so the PDF's upload month is used as the publication bound. 12/12 2026 polls match Wikipedia.
pollsters.status_reason: Meets R1-R4. Pooled waves (weighted base usually 1.3-1.6x respondents, e.g. 2,773 v 2,023; 2.3x on 24-27 Jul) mean consecutive polls share respondents; the average should down-weight accordingly.
open_questions: Question wording and prompt list (not in tables; ask Deltapoll)
pollsters.vi_question_source: Not published: tables give only 'General Election Voting Intention [Excluding 'Don't know' and 'Would not vote']'
pollsters.restore_britain_note: Not shown separately in any 2026 table (inside Other); whether it is prompted is not published.
pollsters.turnout_threshold: New turnout model (method note May 2026); tables base 'All adults in GB who intend to vote'

pollsters.name: YouGov
pollsters.bpc_evidence: Results PDF: "YouGov is a member of the British Polling Council and abides by its rules."
pollsters.vi_question: Now, thinking specifically about your own constituency, if there were a general election held tomorrow and these were the parties standing, which party would you vote for?
pollsters.vi_question_source: Results PDF (drives the headline). A generic question is asked first: 'If there were a general election held tomorrow, which party would you vote for?'
pollsters.restore_britain_note: Per YouGov's 10 Mar 2026 method note, small parties are left out of the main prompt and collected via 'other'.
pollsters.reuse_terms: Public data licence (updated 7 Mar 2025): CC BY-NC 4.0; commercial use needs written consent; "You may not use bots, crawlers, or automated scripts to extract or copy the Licensed Data without our express written permission."
pollsters.scrape_notes: Content API (politics category) lists weekly 'voting-intention-...' articles from 10 Mar 2026; each links a results PDF (VotingIntention_Results_/MRP_/MRP_Results_ YYMMDD). PDF layout varies week to week; parser reads columns from each page and falls back to pypdf layout mode when numbers run together. Tracker xlsx (api-test.yougov.com .../trackers/voting-intention/download/) gives rounded headlines + crossbreaks weekly from Jan 2025; used for headline-only backfill and as a cross-check (36/36 PDF weeks agree).
pollsters.status_reason: Meets R1-R4. Scraped under the Times' agreement. Treated identically to every other firm in the average, and the page should say so.
open_questions: Headline method for Jan 2025-Mar 2026 tracker weeks (pre-dates the method note)
pollsters.scrape_permission: User confirmed 13 Nov 2026 that the Times' agreement with YouGov permits scraping; YouGov's public licence otherwise bars automated extraction.
pollsters.second_screen_question: And which of these parties would you vote for? [Asked only to those who said 'Some other party']
pollsters.turnout_threshold: Modelled in the MRP from demographics and past turnout by group, not from stated likelihood (method note, 10 Mar 2026)
pollsters.dk_text: The MRP model reallocates don't knows to vote like people with the same demographics and past vote (method note, 10 Mar 2026).
pollsters.headline_method: MRP projection to GB from the constituency question
pollsters.weighting_text: YouGov weights GB political surveys by (1) age interlocked with gender and education, (2) political attention (3) social grade (4) 2024 recalled vote interlocked with region (5) EU referendum recalled vote and (6) ethnicity. ... Voting intention figures are seperately modelled using MRP.
pollsters.crossbreaks: Vote in 2024 GE; EU Ref 2016; Gender; Age (18-24, 25-49, 50-64, 65+); NS-SEC (Higher, Intermediate, Routine); Country; Region in England (North, Midlands, London, Rest of South)

pollsters.name: Trajectory Partnership
pollsters.bpc_evidence: Poll web page: "Trajectory are members of the British Polling Council and all polls are conducted in accordance with their rules."
pollsters.weighting_text: Data are collected using quotas. Weighted to be representative of GE 2024 turnout and voting.
pollsters.turnout_question: 0-10 certainty to vote (wording not in the PDF tables)
pollsters.turnout_threshold: 6/10 or above (methodology page 01.07.2026). Tables also show 10/10, 8-10 and registered-to-vote columns.
pollsters.vi_question: If there were a general election held tomorrow, which party would you vote for?
pollsters.headline_table: TABLE 1. Two headlines published: 'All giving voting intention' and 'All likely to vote (6/10+)'. Wikipedia uses the likely-to-vote column.

pollsters.tables_format: pdf (2 pages, exported from Excel; pypdf text extraction works)

Implemented via WordPress posts API (search 'optimism index'). Feb-Apr 2026 layout has no VI-base columns; headline then from the 6-10 likelihood column, party shares of party counts. Rows with blank cells (WNV/DK/refused) kept out of crossbreaks.
pollsters.status_reason: Meets R1-R4 (just: monthly). Use the likely-to-vote (6/10+) column as headline.
pollsters.weighting_note: Feb-May 2026 PDFs state 'Data are collected using quotas. Unweighted.'; weighted to GE2024 turnout and vote from July 2026. Polls flagged weighted=false.

pollsters.name: Lord Ashcroft Polls
pollsters.bpc_evidence: No BPC statement in tables or articles; Wikipedia footnotes rows as non-BPC
pollsters.turnout_question: Many people say they won’t vote at the next general election, while others say they definitely will. On a scale of 0 (certain NOT to vote) to 10 (absolutely certain to vote), how likely are you to vote at the next general election?
pollsters.vi_question: As things stand today, how likely would you say it is that you will end up voting for each of the following parties at the next election - where 0 means “there is no chance I will vote for that party”, and 100 means “I will definitely vote for that party”.
pollsters.vi_derivation_text: Based on the highest score respondents gave for any party that was more than 50. Cases that gave no party a score of 50 or more were coded as 'don't know / would not vote'. Asked to those who said they would be likely to vote in the previous question; n=4854. Weighted by turnout weight
pollsters.crossbreaks: Current VI; 2024 vote; 2019 vote; EU ref; Con 2019; Lab 2024; Gender; Age; NS-SEC; Social grade; Region; Country; Region in England
pollsters.status_reason: Fails R2: VI is derived from 0-100 propensity scores, not a direct party choice question, and Restore Britain is not among the parties rated. Show in the poll list, keep out of the average. Also not a BPC member.

pollsters.name: BMG Research
pollsters.bpc_evidence: Tables methodology sheet: "BMG Research is a Company Partner of the Market Research Society (MRS), member of the British Polling Council (BPC) and abides by their rules."
pollsters.weighting_text: Targets were Age/Sex, Parliamentary Constituency, Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD), Education, the 2024 General Election results and the 2016 EU Referendum results.
pollsters.turnout_question: On a scale of 0 to 10, where 0 means you definitely won't vote and 10 means you definitely will vote, how likely would you be to vote at a General Election if it was held today?
pollsters.turnout_threshold: LTV asked; VI base 'Where not Definitely will not vote'. Plus an electoral registration adjustment by age and tenure.
pollsters.vi_question: If a General Election were held today, which of the following parties would you vote for?
pollsters.squeeze_question: And which of the following parties are you leaning towards most?
pollsters.dk_text: squeeze responses are re-allocated and given a weighting factor of 0.75. Where no party is selected at squeeze question a factor of 0.5 is allocated based on how they previously voted in 2024 General Election.
pollsters.headline_table: WouldVoteTodayRevised, base 'Not sure and prefer not to say removed' (after squeeze and registration factors)
pollsters.crossbreaks: Past vote (2024) and others; WinCross export with significance letters in alternate rows
pollsters.tables_format: xlsx (WinCross export; Cover, Methodology sheet, Index, Tables)
pollsters.reuse_terms: Site terms: "You must not use any part of the content on our site for commercial purposes without obtaining a licence to do so from us or our licensors."
pollsters.scrape_notes: Significance-letter rows interleave with data rows. Same question appears in several tables with different bases; pick the final one. Implemented via WordPress media API ('the-i'); each step of the VI chain (raw, LTV factors, squeeze, registration, DK removed) stored as its own question.

pollsters.name: Ipsos UK (Political Monitor)
pollsters.bpc_evidence: Not stated on pages read (long-standing member; confirm)
pollsters.panel_provider: Ipsos KnowledgePanel (address-based random probability recruitment; switched from phone in June 2025)
pollsters.weighting_text: Design weights, then rim weights to age and gender, region, ethnicity, qualifications, work status and sector, social grade, cars in household, constituency type, newspaper readership (from release text). Sample stratified by 2024 vote.

pollsters.squeeze_question: Which party are you most inclined to support? (General Election tomorrow)

pollsters.headline_table: V1AB/V2 COMBINED VOTING INTENTION - LIKELY TO VOTE
pollsters.crossbreaks: Ethnicity; social grade (AB, C1, C2, DE, ABC1, C2DE); age (18-34, 35-49, 50-64, 65+); gender; likelihood to vote; qualifications; 2024 vote; ONS regions; tenure; work sector; government satisfaction; working status; current VI
pollsters.tables_format: pdf (63 pages; text extraction merges columns, needs a layout-aware parser)
pollsters.reuse_terms: "Polls appearing on this website are deemed to be in the public domain and therefore may be used in whole or in part as long as attribution is made" (but a separate copyright clause forbids reproduction without permission)
pollsters.scrape_notes: Site search (server-rendered) plus tables PDFs cited on Wikipedia's polling page as discovery seeds (search misses releases; PDF names vary: 'Political Monitor Tables <Month>', 'politmkp_w8sep2026web1'). System Python's LibreSSL can't negotiate ipsos.com TLS; common.get falls back to curl.
pollsters.status_reason: Meets R1-R4 (monthly). The only probability-panel poll, which makes it a useful anchor.
pollsters.extraction_note: Full crosstabs since 14 Nov 2026: four VI tables (V1AB/V2 all and likely-to-vote, V1AB, V2) by 57 crossbreak columns, read from positioned text fragments of the rotated PDF. Percentages recomputed from whole-number weighted counts (can differ from printed % by 1pt in small cells). Headline = party count over 'Total voting (sub-base)'.
